blocks.note: the Cuban leader's surname, taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star is cast in the role of Fidel Castro.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is the second brightest star in the Gemini constellation, twin to Pollux.

indicators.note: when the wife leaves, her abbreviation departs from the word that follows

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a wally is British slang for a silly, foolish person

explanation.surface: A woman walks out on her foolish husband in favour of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY loses its W to give ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or partner on your side, a close synonym for a friend.

blocks.note: surface reading: queueing, getting in a row
setter's reading: a cord stretched high in the air for a performer to walk along

explanation.surface: Performers queue to take their turn at a balancing act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line up' reads as a verb meaning queue, but it is a noun phrase: a line strung up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus walker balances on a taut cord raised above the ground, literally an elevated line.

clue.text: Give Browning, say, a new lease of life (or death!)

definitions.text: Give Browning, say, a new lease of life (or death!)

blocks.clueFragment: Give Browning, say, a new lease of life
blocks.note: surface reading: reviving the reputation of the poet Robert Browning

blocks.clueFragment: Browning, say, a new lease of life (or death!)
blocks.note: setter's reading: a Browning is a make of firearm, given fresh ammunition so it can kill again

explanation.surface: Someone revives interest in the Victorian poet Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet, but it is the gun maker; putting in new cartridges gives the weapon renewed power to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To put fresh ammunition into a gun after firing is exactly what this verb means.

indicators.note: could be says the following letters might become something else if rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree described as possibly very creamy in colour or texture.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large broadleaved maple species common in Britain and Europe.

clue.text: I left Sparta in distress, waving flag

indicators.note: left here means departed, so one letter goes out of the phrase
waving suggests letters fluttering about and settling into a new order

blocks.note: the letter to be removed
taken as written, sixteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone flees a troubled Sparta, waving a flag as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from SPARTA IN DISTRESS, then rearrange the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the popular name of the national banner of the United States.

clue.text: Cyril and Leo playing in coalmine

indicators.note: playing implies the two names are frolicking around and mixing their letters together

blocks.note: the two names, taken as written

explanation.surface: Two boys named Cyril and Leo are playing down a coalmine.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal pit together with its surface buildings, the British term for a mine.

clue.text: He used sorcery - a mug's game!

indicators.note: game in the sense of lame or crippled, so the letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on witchcraft: practising magic is only for fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mug's game' is a fixed British phrase for a foolish pursuit, here split into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a magician or sorcerer, originally a member of the Persian priestly caste.

indicators.note: amended means corrected or altered, so the letters are put into a revised order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tax return has its mistakes corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrogress is to go back to an earlier, usually worse, state, a verb meaning revert.

blocks.note: a flag is a common name for an iris plant
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A question whether whips were made by a woman called Iris Fitzgerald.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a first name, but it is the plant; Fitzgerald stands for the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagella are the lashing, whip-like appendages microbes use for swimming; the word is Latin for small whips.

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: light as in a pale colour
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sodium lamps glow pale as they start up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sodium tempts you towards its chemical symbol Na, but only its first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Flares are bright signal lamps or burning beacons, so they are kinds of illumination sources.

clue.text: Trains miss out on delivery system

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or put out of place

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cancelled trains mean deliveries do not arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' sits in the middle of the fodder and reads as part of 'miss out on'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vehicle the gearbox and drive shafts form the mechanism that conveys engine power to the wheels.

clue.text: Study of devils does me only good!

indicators.note: does in the sense of cooks or fixes up, so the following letters are worked over

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that studying demons is beneficial for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal, as in a cook doing the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonology is the scholarly field concerned with beliefs about evil spirits and fiends.

indicators.note: among says the letters sit in the midst of the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A lion in an amphitheatre, among the ancient Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: Lion suggests Roman arenas, but here it means a celebrated person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion can be a celebrity, someone lionised; a hero is similarly a much admired figure.

blocks.note: 17 across is BOREALIS, Latin for northern
corona is Latin for crown

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue naming a constellation from its Latin parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The constellation Corona Borealis is translated word by word into English; the two halves swap order to read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern Crown is the English name of Corona Borealis, a small semicircular group of stars.

clue.text: Difficult case for the rigidly orthodox

blocks.note: hard means difficult
a shell is an outer case or casing

explanation.surface: A tough legal case for strict traditionalists to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a legal problem, but it means a casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-shell describes people who are uncompromising and strict in belief, originally certain Baptists in America.

clue.text: Amazing saves made by unsighted goalkeeper?

blocks.note: first meaning: a blinder is British slang for an outstanding piece of play
second meaning, playfully: keepers who cannot see, people who are blind

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper who could not even see the ball still made brilliant saves.
explanation.walkthrough: To play a blinder is British slang for performing brilliantly; the question mark flags the jokey second sense of 'blind ones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacular performances are called blinders in British sport, and a whimsical coinage makes blind people blinders too.

clue.text: 14 10 could, perhaps, be sailor stealing Aurora

definitions.note: the word is what remains of Aurora Borealis, the northern lights, once Aurora is stolen away

indicators.note: could perhaps be signals that the following letters might form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea steals a glimpse of the dawn goddess Aurora and the northern lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 10 is NORTHERN LIGHTS, whose Latin name is Aurora Borealis; take away Aurora and BOREALIS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Borealis is Latin for northern, the second word in the scientific name for the polar light display.

clue.text: What is left of the spider?

blocks.note: first meaning: the remainder
second meaning: in snooker, the spider is a raised cue support

explanation.surface: A grisly question about the remains of a squashed spider.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a rest is a stick that supports the cue, and the spider is one kind with a raised head.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the other things left over, and a snooker spider is a type of cue support.

blocks.note: a stir is a commotion
up means aloft

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble among those in positions of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High places' suggests powerful people, but it simply means aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble is to incite or provoke it, a common phrasal verb.

blocks.note: surface reading: key excerpts taken from newspapers
setter's reading: strong juices squeezed out in a fruit press, with the water reduced

explanation.surface: A digest of the most important newspaper excerpts.
explanation.walkthrough: The press looks like journalism, but it is a juice press, and essential means distilled to its essence.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrates are liquids reduced to their strongest essence, such as fruit juices squeezed and thickened.

indicators.note: in says the letters are contained within the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Jacob's brother relaxing in a sauna.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Bible describes Jacob's brother as a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau is the elder twin of Jacob who sold his birthright for a dish of stew.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or put out of place

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Rooms painted blue somewhere out in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means sad or gloomy, and morose describes a sullen, melancholy mood.

clue.text: Unreasonable way of paying a poet?

blocks.note: first meaning: contrary, obstinately wrong
second meaning, punning: a fee for each stanza written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a method of paying a poet is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PER VERSE, a rate charged for every stanza; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means stubbornly contrary or against reason, behaving in a deliberately unreasonable way.

clue.text: Athletes who cover the floor supply

definitions.text: Athletes who cover the floor supply

blocks.note: surface reading: carpet fitters who provide flooring

blocks.clueFragment: Athletes who cover the floor supply
blocks.note: setter's reading: sportspeople who move over the floor exercise mat supplely, that is in a supple way

explanation.surface: Athletes who lay down a supply of floor coverings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as provide, but it is the adverb of supple, describing how these athletes perform their floor routines.
explanation.definitionFit: In artistic competition these sportspeople perform floor routines requiring great flexibility and agility.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the preceding word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut back on' reads as reduce, but 'on' just places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollux is the brightest star in the Gemini constellation, twin of Castor.
